title: 16-06-pace-code-c-2015.pdf — section 97
text:
16.7 When a juvenile is charged with an offence and the custody officer
authorises their continued detention after charge, the custody
officer must try to make arrangements for the juvenile to be taken
to a place of safety, other than a police station, within the
meaning of Article 39(8) of the Police and Criminal Evidence
(Northern Ireland) Order 1989 to be detained pending appearance
in court unless the custody officer certifies it is impracticable to
do so or no secure accommodation is available and there is a risk
to the public of serious harm from that juvenile, in accordance
with Article 39(6) of the Police and Criminal Evidence (Northern
Ireland) Order 1989. See Note 16C.
16.7A The requirement in paragraph 3.4(b) that documents and materials
essential to effectively challenging the lawfulness of the
detainee’s arrest and detention must be made available to the
 64
detainee and, if they are represented, their solicitor, applies for
the purposes of this section and a person’s detention after charge.
This means that the custody officer making the bail decision
(PACE, Article 39) or reviewing the need for detention after charge
(PACE, Article 41), is responsible for determining what, if any,
documents or materials are essential and must be made available
to the detainee or their solicitor. See Note 3A.
